{{short description|Design method for cryptographic hash functions}}

The '''HAIFA construction''' (''hash iterative framework'') is a cryptographic structure used in the design of [[Cryptographic hash function|hash functions]]. It is one of the modern alternatives to the [[Merkle–Damgård construction]],<ref>{{Cite conference|last=Biham|first=Eli|last2=Dunkelman|first2=Orr|date=24 August 2006|title=A Framework for Iterative Hash Functions - HAIFA|url=https://eprint.iacr.org/2007/278|conference=Second NIST Cryptographic Hash Workshop|via=Cryptology ePrint Archive: Report 2007/278}}</ref> avoiding its weaknesses like [[length extension attack]]s. The construction was designed by [[Eli Biham]] and [[Orr Dunkelman]] in 2007.

Three of the 14 second round candidates in the [[NIST hash function competition]] were based on HAIFA constructions ([[BLAKE (hash function)|BLAKE]], SHAvite-3, ECHO). Other hash functions based on it are LAKE, Sarmal, [[SWIFFT|SWIFFTX]] and HNF-256. The construction of [[Skein (hash function)|Skein]] ([[Unique Block Iteration]]) is similar to HAIFA.<ref>Jean-Philippe Aumasson, Willi Meier, Raphael Phan, Luca Henzen: ''The Hash Function BLAKE'', p. 35</ref> Another alternative construction is the [[sponge construction]].
